title: Sona's ten children
hookLine: a mother of ten, left alone in old age, goes forth and awakens

cards: Her poem opens with a number. Ten children, she says, I bore from this body. Her name is Sona.
The commentary fills in the rest. Her husband leaves home for the homeless life, and she divides the family wealth among her children, keeping nothing back.

Once there's nothing more to hand out, the children stop caring for her. She is old now, weak, and alone in the house she filled. So, with nothing left to give away, she goes to the nuns and asks to begin.

teach.b: First, her own verses, in the Therigatha. After bearing her children, Sona says, weak and grown old, she went to a nun. The nun taught her the aggregates, the sense bases and the elements, and she went forth.
Second, the work. The commentary says she knew she had started late, so she resolved to practice through the day and through the night, as though there were no time to spare.
One day the other nuns went out and left her behind to heat the water for their baths.
While the water warmed, she walked up and down in walking meditation, and there, the story says, beside the fire and the pot, she woke. Third, her title.
In the list of foremost disciples, Sona is named first among the nuns who put forth energy. The title goes to the old mother who started last and was left to mind the water.
Fourth, where her poem ends. She speaks of her mind as freed and her task as done. It isn't really a story about ungrateful children; they barely appear.
It's about what she did with what was left: a tired body, a late start, a pot of water to heat. She didn't wait to be young again. She began where she was.

how: Sona's verses are read in the Therigatha, and in the Theravada tradition she is remembered by her title, foremost among nuns in energy, together with the story of her late start.

o: calm, a mind that has settled down
energy, effort that doesn't give up

p: named in the first line of her poem
what Sona was left to heat

s: Sona went forth when she was young
she went forth old and weak, after raising her children.
the Buddha's list names Sona foremost in energy
first among the nuns who put forth energy.
the story is mostly about her children's ingratitude
they barely appear. it's about what she did with a late start.

games.q: you're old and newly a nun. the others go out and leave you to heat their bath water. what do you do?
o: heat it, and stew over being left behind.
heat it, and practice walking meditation while it warms.
games.why: the commentary says she practiced walking meditation while the water heated, and woke right there.

practice: Picture an older person who started something late: learned to read or swim, went back to school, took up a practice, learned a new country's language.
Hold them in mind with respect, and wonder what it took to begin in front of people half their age. If something in you has been waiting for the right age, let that be noticed too, just noticed.

wordCard.voice: Viriya, energy or effort. The quality Sona was named foremost in, after going forth late and practicing as though there were no time to spare. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali viriya, energy or effort: the quality Sona is named foremost in.

carryVoice: Your line: never too late. A late start was still a start. Day seven hundred sixty-one, done.
